400 Rail RD
Newtown

19/04/2015

Dear Dr Jones,

Re: Mrs. Patricia Welshman                              DOB 28/03/1930



   I am writing to refer Mrs. Welshman, a-85-year- old widow, whose symptoms and signs
are suggestive of dementia. Your effort would be highly appreciated.                            Comment [teacher1]: assessment

Mrs. Welshman lives alone. She was diagnosed with osteoporosis. Moreover, she has a family      Comment [teacher2]: and suffers from
history of Alzheimer’s.

On 14/12/2014, the patient’s blood pressure was mildly elevated. Thus, some laboratory
tests were ordered. The results showed only a high LDL cholesterol level at 2.9mmol/L and a
low vitamin D concentration at 54mmol/L. The patient showed a poor commitment to spare          Comment [teacher3]: medicine
scripts. However, she reported taking all medications in time. Webester pack was                Comment [teacher4]: without her realizing it.
recommended, but the patient refused it. 2 months later, while the LDL cholesterol level        Comment [teacher5]: So, a Webster
increased significantly, the vitamin D concentration declined considerably. Consequently, she
agreed to depend on Webester pack.                                                              Comment [teacher6]: use a Webster

    Today, the patient presented with a poor memory, including not remembering to do            Comment [teacher7]: with her daughter and both were
                                                                                                concerned about her
some daily activities, such as dinner engagements and missing social events along with some
                                                                                                Comment [teacher8]: as she was forgetting about
behavioural changes. The mini memory assessment revealed a poor short memory towards
the date. Although she could not remember the current day and month, she could confirm
the year. Finally, the difference between dementia, which is a symptom, and Alzheimer’s, the    Comment [teacher9]: a
cause of dementia, was discussed.

  On light of the above, the patient is being referred for further memory assessment before     Comment [teacher10]: In

  Yours sincerely,

    Doctor
